This is one of those games that are sooooo challenging and unforgiving. 
But man oh man the feeling of achievement! How satisfying it is once you complete a playthrough for the first time! No better reward.
Cause indeed this game doesn't keep generating procedural levels until you die, getting harder and harder every second that goes by! It actually has an end, one that you can reach.
Leave the casual behind, this world is harsh, and you will die. Oh yeah.
But keep learning, never stop fighting, don't even think about lowering your guard and you'll see this game has a lot to offer.
Not that pleasing on the eye but with its own graphic style, you will never get bored.
The only drawback that I can think of is the difficulty one has to join a game. You can't actually join a friend's game through Steam, you have to enter the IP address. Hopefully this will be improved in the future.
Play it, love it, hate it after a stupid mistake that cost your life, love it even more, but don't miss it.

I was looking through my library of games on Steam to see which one I've played the most, and Risk of Rain takes the cake. I've played this game 40% more than my second most played game. So, I figured, it deserves a nice review from me.

I bought Risk of Rain in a steam sale (like everyone does) a while back when it was something like 75% off. I was honestly just looking for something I could pick up and play for a few hours and then probably never touch again. Despite the positive reviews I had quickly skimmed through, I still was skeptical because I've never liked a single rogue-like game besides Binding of Isaac. In most rogue-likes, once I die 5 or 6 times I usually rage-quit and never play it again. But when I booted up Risk of Rain, I was immediately blown away. The first thing I noticed was the music. The music from the first levels is always very mysterious. It got me to feel just as curious as the character I'm playing as is supposed to be. What planet is this? Who was that guy that crashed the ship I was on? What am I supposed to do? Then, as you progress through the levels, the music picks up as you become more and more determined to reach the end and escape this harsh and hostile world!

The game has a lot of replay value. 

First, randomized items and enemies (unless you have certain acquired artifacts turned on). 

Second, decisions. In Risk of Rain you decide whether to kill more enemies for money to open more chests, or go straight for the exit. And the balance between the two is still something I'm figuring out after having played for over 130 hours. I should also add that the mechanic of having to wait 90 seconds for the transporter to turn on while a high influx of waves come at you (including a boss) is AWESOME and creates many tense moments.

Third, length of the game. The game is just long enough that you don't feel helpless as you try again and again, and beating the game is feasible. 

Fourth, character variety. The only thing I think you could complain about is also the one thing I happen to like about the game. That is, the characters are not balanced at all. Some are much easier than others. I personally find the huntress to be the easiest to beat the game with, as she can run and shoot at the same time, making it easy to kite enemies. And then I find the sniper's abilities to be really tough to master, and Acrid's melee abilities are hard to close-in with without taking damage. I think that this actually adds to the game. You may find other characters easier depending on your play-style, thereby making more options to present yourself with different difficulty levels.

	All in all, the game is great. I highly recommend it, even at full price. It's a fun game you can get into, play for a bit, leave, and pick back up again the next day. I've been addicted for a while now, and I don't get tired of it. The music's very fitting, the graphics are pleasantly simple, the game-play is thrilling, and no two attempts are the same. That sinking feeling you get when you know you're about to die after how far you've come is absolutely the worst, and keeps me motivated to get better.
Tons of fun when you get into it.. vary addictive xD

*Short and to the pont*

This game is amazingly fun. It is difficult yet not too difficult. The way new heros unlocks is very rewarding and you always feel like you are progresisng. Also boss fights are great, sometimes they can be just absurdly difficult depending on how many people are in game or what class you are playing. I recommend playing it with 2-3 of your friends. Solo play can get a little boring to be honest.

Personally I don't like this game by itself very much, However I do believe that the multiplayer makes it an amazing expeirience no mater how many times you've played it through there's something about sitting in a room with your friends playing this game and attempting to make it to the end of each level enduring the difficulties
